projects_core.name: projects_core
projects_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  unics_id,
  acronym,
  title,
  ec_call,
  ec_fund_scheme,
  cordis_ref,
  ec_ref,
  start_date,
  end_date,
  start_year,
  end_year,
  homepage,
  total_cost,
  ec_max_contribution,
  framework_program,
  objective,
  principal_investigator
FROM projects

params.description: Provides one-row-per-project core attributes and financial totals (project-level metadata and aggregate cost/contribution fields).
params.when_to_use: Look up project-level metadata (title, acronym, identifiers, dates, homepage, objective, PI) for a specific project (by unics_id or other identifier). | Build dashboards or reports that list projects with their total cost and EC maximum contribution alongside basic metadata. | Serve as the base (one-row-per-project) for composing additional aggregations or joins to participant, year, location, or ranking data — when you need to preserve project-level cardinality.
params.output_schema: unics_id: unique project identifier — directly from projects.unics_id | acronym: project short name/acronym — from projects.acronym | title: full project title — from projects.title | ec_call: European Commission call identifier (call name/code) — from projects.ec_call | ec_fund_scheme: EC funding scheme (e.g., FP7, H2020 instrument) — from projects.ec_fund_scheme | cordis_ref: CORDIS reference identifier for the project — from projects.cordis_ref | ec_ref: EC reference identifier (alternative EC ID) — from projects.ec_ref | start_date: project start date (date) — from projects.start_date | end_date: project end date (date) — from projects.end_date | start_year: project start year (integer) — from projects.start_year | end_year: project end year (integer) — from projects.end_year | homepage: project URL/homepage — from projects.homepage | total_cost: project total cost (monetary amount) — from projects.total_cost | ec_max_contribution: maximum EC contribution to the project (monetary amount) — from projects.ec_max_contribution | framework_program: name of the framework program (e.g., FP7, H2020) — from projects.framework_program | objective: project abstract/objective text — from projects.objective | principal_investigator: principal investigator / contact person name or id — from projects.principal_investigator
params.grounded_columns: projects.unics_id | projects.acronym | projects.title | projects.ec_call | projects.ec_fund_scheme | projects.cordis_ref | projects.ec_ref | projects.start_date | projects.end_date | projects.start_year | projects.end_year | projects.homepage | projects.total_cost | projects.ec_max_contribution | projects.framework_program | projects.objective | projects.principal_investigator
params.metric: total_cost = projects.total_cost  -- this is a base numeric column representing the project-level total cost, not an aggregate computed in the view | ec_max_contribution = projects.ec_max_contribution  -- this is a base numeric column representing the EC contribution cap at project-level
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to projects_principal_investigators on unics_id — safe because projects_principal_investigators is expected to be one-row-per-project (or pre-aggregated to one row per unics_id); joining on unics_id will not duplicate this view's project-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to projects_with_programmes_subjects_topics on unics_id — safe if that sibling view is one-row-per-project (it is named as a JOIN view but must be validated as one-row-per-unics_id); if it is one-row-per-project, measures are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to projects_rank_by_total_cost on unics_id — safe because ranking views typically have one row per project; join will not multiply rows. | do NOT directly join to project_members_clean (or project_member_counts_by_country, project_financials_by_member) on unics_id without aggregation — these are one-to-many at the project level (multiple members per project). Directly joining would multiply project rows and duplicate total_cost and ec_max_contribution. Instead, first aggregate member-level views to one row per unics_id (for example SUM/COUNT by unics_id) or join via a pre-aggregated view such as project_member_counts_by_country aggregated to project-level. | do NOT directly join to project_financials_by_member on unics_id without re-aggregation — financials by member are member-level and will duplicate project-level totals. Aggregate financials to project-level (SUM by unics_id) before joining to preserve correct measures. | when composing time-series or year rollups, join to projects_yearly_budget_rollup only if that view is aggregated at project-year (unics_id, year) and you plan to match on both keys (unics_id + year). Joining projects (one row per project) to project-year rows will naturally expand project rows into multiple year rows; this is acceptable when you intend per-year granularity but be mindful that project-level totals (total_cost) represent the whole project and should not be summed again across years without an adjusted allocation. | when joining to institution_locations or erc_panel_assignments (JOIN views), verify their cardinality: if they are one-row-per-project (unics_id) the join is safe; if they are many-to-one or many-to-many, aggregate those sources to one row per unics_id before joining to avoid duplicating project-level fields. | general rule: this view is one-row-per-unics_id. Any join partner that is one-row-per-unics_id (or has been pre-aggregated to that grain) is safe and will not duplicate project-level measures. Any join partner with multiple rows per unics_id will require aggregation (e.g., SUM, COUNT, MAX) to project-level first, or the planner must apply DISTINCT/row_number-based deduplication, to avoid inflating project-level metrics.

projects_core.description: Normalized/cleaned projection of the projects table exposing key identifiers, descriptive attributes, and core measures. Use this as the canonical projects relation for joins, year-based aggregations, and timeline analyses. | Use for: Time-series of projects per start_year or end_year; Budget aggregations (total_cost, ec_max_contribution) by programme/fund scheme; Joining projects to participants or dimensions (institutions, countries, topics)

Show the title of the project with the highest total cost

Find member name and role code of project members in project with acronym GTBB

project_members_clean.name: project_members_clean
project_members_clean.body_sql:
SELECT
  unics_id,
  project,
  pic_number,
  rcn,
  member_name,
  activity_type,
  country,
  street,
  city,
  postal_code,
  ec_contribution,
  institution_id,
  member_role,
  geocode_regions_3,
  member_short_name,
  department_name,
  vat_number,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  region_code,
  region_name
FROM project_members

params.description: One-row-per-project-member normalized view: lists cleaned member-level facts for projects including identifiers, location, role and EC contribution.
params.when_to_use: Get member-level details for a specific project (by project, rcn or pic_number). | Compose member-level reports (e.g., list members, roles, contributions) and then aggregate by project, country, or institution. | Join member attributes to project-level data when you need member granularity (for e.g., computing per-member shares). | Filter or group projects by member characteristics (country, region, department, VAT, geocode regions). | Geospatial mapping of project members using latitude/longitude or region codes.
params.output_schema: unics_id: unique row identifier for this project-member combination — derives from project_members.unics_id | project: project identifier (string) — derives from project_members.project | pic_number: PIC (Participant Identification Code) for the project/member — derives from project_members.pic_number | rcn: RCN (research/record contract number) identifying the project — derives from project_members.rcn | member_name: full legal name of the member/institution — derives from project_members.member_name | activity_type: declared activity type for the member within the project — derives from project_members.activity_type | country: ISO country or country name for the member's location — derives from project_members.country | street: street address for the member/institution — derives from project_members.street | city: city for the member/institution — derives from project_members.city | postal_code: postal code for the member/institution — derives from project_members.postal_code | ec_contribution: EC (European Commission) contribution allocated to this member — derives from project_members.ec_contribution | institution_id: internal institution identifier for the member — derives from project_members.institution_id | member_role: role of the member in the project (e.g., coordinator, partner) — derives from project_members.member_role | geocode_regions_3: administrative/geocode region code (3-level) for the member — derives from project_members.geocode_regions_3 | member_short_name: short display name for the member/institution — derives from project_members.member_short_name | department_name: department within the institution (if available) — derives from project_members.department_name | vat_number: VAT / tax ID for the member/institution — derives from project_members.vat_number | latitude: latitude coordinate for the member location — derives from project_members.latitude | longitude: longitude coordinate for the member location — derives from project_members.longitude | region_code: standardized region code for the member (e.g., NUTS/ISO region) — derives from project_members.region_code | region_name: human-readable region name corresponding to region_code — derives from project_members.region_name
params.grounded_columns: project_members.unics_id | project_members.project | project_members.pic_number | project_members.rcn | project_members.member_name | project_members.activity_type | project_members.country | project_members.street | project_members.city | project_members.postal_code | project_members.ec_contribution | project_members.institution_id | project_members.member_role | project_members.geocode_regions_3 | project_members.member_short_name | project_members.department_name | project_members.vat_number | project_members.latitude | project_members.longitude | project_members.region_code | project_members.region_name
params.metric: ec_contribution = project_members.ec_contribution  -- a base numeric value per project-member (NOT aggregated in this view) | row_count = count(unics_id) when aggregated  -- implicit cardinality metric: this view is normalized at the unics_id (one row per unics_id)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to projects_core on project_members.project = projects_core.project — safe because this view is one-row-per-member; projects_core is one-row-per-project, so project attributes will be added without duplicating member rows or ec_contribution. | cardinality-SAFE: join to project_principal_investigators (projects_principal_investigators) on project_members.project = projects_principal_investigators.project — safe if you only need PI attributes (one-row-per-project); PI fields will not duplicate member-level rows. | cardinality-SAFE: join to institution_locations on project_members.institution_id = institution_locations.institution_id when institution_locations is one-row-per-institution — safe to enrich institutional address/canonical coordinates without duplicating member measures. | DO NOT join without re-aggregation to one-to-many child tables/views (e.g., project_financials_by_member or project_member_counts_by_country) directly on project key expecting preserved measures — joining this member view to another view that is one-to-many per project-member (or per project) will multiply rows and sum-like measures unless you aggregate first. | If you need to combine with aggregate views (project_financials_by_member, projects_yearly_budget_rollup, project_member_counts_by_country, projects_rank_by_total_cost): either (a) aggregate project_members_clean to the same grain as the target view (e.g., project-level sums of ec_contribution), or (b) join on a unique key that matches the target view's grain (for example join project-level aggregates by project to avoid duplication). | When enriching with JOIN views that are many-to-many (e.g., projects_with_programmes_subjects_topics which may have multiple subjects per project): first reduce that view to a single row per project (choose aggregation or pick preferred subject) or aggregate project_members_clean to the same grouping before joining, otherwise ec_contribution and member counts will be duplicated. | Planner guidance: treat ec_contribution in this view as a member-level atomic measure. Any join that preserves the one-row-per-unics_id property (1-to-1 or many-to-1 from this view's perspective) is safe. Any join that introduces multiple rows per unics_id requires re-aggregation (SUM(ec_contribution) with GROUP BY keys you intend to report) to avoid inflating contributions.

project_members_clean.description: Cleaned projection of project_members exposing participant-level financials, location, and role. Keeps identifiers needed for joins to projects and institutions. | Use for: Aggregate participant contributions per project or country; Map participant institutions to regions and compute regional participation; Filter members by member_role or activity_type

Show the project title and member name where the member has a partner role

projects_with_programmes_subjects_topics.name: projects_with_programmes_subjects_topics
projects_with_programmes_subjects_topics.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id AS unics_id,
  p.acronym AS acronym,
  p.title AS title,
  pp.programme AS programme,
  psa.subject_area AS subject_area,
  pt.topic AS topic
FROM projects p
LEFT JOIN project_programmes pp ON pp.project = p.unics_id
LEFT JOIN project_subject_areas psa ON psa.project = p.unics_id
LEFT JOIN project_topics pt ON pt.project = p.unics_id

params.description: Lists projects with their associated programme(s), subject area(s), and topic(s) at the per-project × programme × subject_area × topic grain.
params.when_to_use: Show all programmes, subject areas and topics linked to each project (including projects that have none for any of these dimensions). | Filter or aggregate projects by programme, subject area, or topic (e.g., count projects per programme×subject or budget rollups later) while preserving the combinatorial associations. | Use as a building block when composing higher-level aggregates (project counts, budget sums) grouped by programme, subject_area, or topic — but ensure you re-aggregate after joining to avoid double-counting.
params.output_schema: unics_id: Project unique identifier, derived from projects.unics_id | acronym: Project acronym, derived from projects.acronym | title: Project title, derived from projects.title | programme: Programme name/code associated to the project, derived from project_programmes.programme | subject_area: Subject area name/code associated to the project, derived from project_subject_areas.subject_area | topic: Topic name/code associated to the project, derived from project_topics.topic
params.grounded_columns: projects.unics_id | projects.acronym | projects.title | project_programmes.project | project_programmes.programme | project_subject_areas.project | project_subject_areas.subject_area | project_topics.project | project_topics.topic
params.metric: This view contains no aggregated numeric metrics. All outputs are base attributes (no derived aggregates). If you need project counts or budget sums after using this view, define derived metrics such as: | project_count = COUNT(DISTINCT unics_id)  -- count of distinct projects in the composed result | sum_budget = SUM(budget)  -- only valid after joining a budget-containing view/table at a 1:1 project grain or after aggregating budgets to the same grain (see composition guidance)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to projects_core on projects_core.unics_id = projects_with_programmes_subjects_topics.unics_id — safe because projects_core is one-row-per-project (NORM) so it will not duplicate rows from this view when joined by unics_id. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to projects_principal_investigators on projects_principal_investigators.unics_id = projects_with_programmes_subjects_topics.unics_id — only safe if the principal_investigators view is one-row-per-project (check its grain). If that view is one-row-per-project (JOIN), it's safe; if it is one-to-many, re-aggregate before joining. | DO NOT join this view directly to one-to-many tables/views such as project_members_clean, project_financials_by_member, project_member_counts_by_country, or projects_yearly_budget_rollup without re-aggregation, because those are many-rows-per-project (NORM or AGG at member or year/member grain) and will multiply this view's rows and thus duplicate any measures derived from project-level attributes. | If you need to combine with a many-rows-per-project source (for example to sum budgets by programme), first aggregate that source to the same grain as this view (project-level or programme×subject_area×topic) — e.g., from project_financials_by_member produce project-level SUM(budget) GROUP BY unics_id, then join on unics_id; or produce SUM(budget) GROUP BY unics_id, programme to join directly without duplication. | When composing aggregates that count projects from this view, prefer COUNT(DISTINCT projects_with_programmes_subjects_topics.unics_id) if joins could introduce multiplicity from other relations; alternatively, aggregate to the desired grain (programme, subject_area, topic, or combinations) by deduplicating unics_id before summing other metrics. | Joining to sibling aggregated views that are already at the same multi-dimensional grain (e.g., a hypothetical projects_by_programme_subject_topic AGG) is safe if that view explicitly uses the identical grain ['unics_id','programme','subject_area','topic'] — otherwise align grains by aggregating the many-side to this view's grain before joining.

projects_with_programmes_subjects_topics.description: Denormalized view joining projects to their programmes, subject areas, and topics. One row per project-per-linked-value for each bridge; useful for filtering or grouping by programme/subject/topic. Preserve keys to enable downstream aggregation or de-duplication. | Use for: Count projects per programme/subject/topic; Find projects associated with a combination of programme and subject area; Filter projects by topic

project_financials_by_member.name: project_financials_by_member
project_financials_by_member.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.project AS project,
  pm.unics_id AS unics_id,
  SUM(pm.ec_contribution) AS total_ec_contribution_by_member,
  COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY pm.project) AS member_count_in_project
FROM project_members pm
GROUP BY pm.project, pm.unics_id

params.description: Per-project, per-member aggregated financial contributions and the number of members in each project (one row per project + member).
params.when_to_use: Get the total EC contribution by a specific member within a specific project. | Compare contributions of different members inside the same project. | Compose per-member contribution metrics with project-level or member-level dimensions (e.g., project metadata, member attributes) while preserving correct aggregation. | Build higher-level aggregates (e.g., project total EC contribution) by summing the per-member totals, or compute per-member share = total_ec_contribution_by_member / member_count_in_project.
params.output_schema: project: project identifier — derives from project_members.project (base column pm.project) used as grouping key. | unics_id: member identifier — derives from project_members.unics_id (base column pm.unics_id) used as grouping key. | total_ec_contribution_by_member: total EC contribution amount for this (project, unics_id) pair — derives from SUM(pm.ec_contribution) aggregated over rows in project_members for the given project and unics_id. | member_count_in_project: number of project members for the project — derives from COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY pm.project) computed over project_members rows for the given project (a window count repeated for each member row within the project).
params.metric: total_ec_contribution_by_member = SUM(project_members.ec_contribution) GROUP BY project_members.project, project_members.unics_id | member_count_in_project = COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY project_members.project)  -- windowed count of rows (members) per project
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to projects_core (or any one-row-per-project dimension) on project = projects_core.project_id (or appropriate project key) — safe because this view is one row per (project, unics_id) and joining on project to a single-row-per-project dimension will not duplicate the measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a member/person dimension (one-row-per-unics_id) on unics_id = member.unics_id — safe because the dimension is one row per unics_id, so total_ec_contribution_by_member and member_count_in_project are not duplicated. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views (for example: a table of multiple location records per project, or any join that is many-rows-per-(project or unics_id)) without re-aggregating afterwards — such joins would duplicate total_ec_contribution_by_member and member_count_in_project. If you must join to a one-to-many relation, either: | - aggregate the many-side to one row per project (or per unics_id) before joining, or | - join and then re-aggregate/group by project and unics_id to restore correct totals. | Examples of unsafe joins without re-aggregation: joining to institution_locations if it contains multiple locations per project/institution; joining to any event/transaction table keyed to project that has multiple rows per project. These would multiply rows for a given (project, unics_id) and thereby inflate SUM-based metrics. | When composing upward (building project-level totals): compute project total EC contribution by SUM(total_ec_contribution_by_member) grouped by project (this is safe because total_ec_contribution_by_member is already per (project,unics_id)). | When composing member-share metrics: compute total_ec_contribution_by_member / NULLIF(member_count_in_project,0) to get average or per-member share; if combining with other aggregated measures, ensure grouping keys align (group by project and/or unics_id as needed).

project_financials_by_member.description: Aggregated financial measures at the project-member and project level: sum of ec_contribution per project and per project-member, plus member counts per project. Useful for budget breakdowns and per-member contribution analysis. | Use for: Total participant EC contribution per project; Share of project budget per participant (join to projects_core.total_cost); Projects with many participants

projects_yearly_budget_rollup.name: projects_yearly_budget_rollup
projects_yearly_budget_rollup.body_sql:
SELECT
  start_year,
  framework_program,
  COUNT(unics_id) AS projects_count,
  SUM(total_cost) AS total_cost_sum,
  SUM(ec_max_contribution) AS ec_max_contribution_sum
FROM projects
GROUP BY start_year, framework_program

params.description: Yearly roll-up of projects by start year and framework program, with counts and summed financials.
params.when_to_use: Total number of projects and aggregated financials (total_cost, ec_max_contribution) per project start year and framework program. | Time-series or cross-program comparisons of project counts and budget totals at the year x framework_program grain. | As a pre-aggregated source when composing higher-level dashboards that need projects_count, total_cost_sum, or ec_max_contribution_sum by year and program. | As an aggregation building block to join to dimension tables (e.g., program labels or year metadata) without re-aggregating.
params.output_schema: start_year: project start year (derived from projects.start_year) | framework_program: framework programme identifier/category (derived from projects.framework_program) | projects_count: count of distinct project rows in this group (COUNT(unics_id) from projects.unics_id) | total_cost_sum: sum of total project cost for the group (SUM(total_cost) from projects.total_cost) | ec_max_contribution_sum: sum of EC max contribution for the group (SUM(ec_max_contribution) from projects.ec_max_contribution)
params.metric: projects_count = COUNT(unics_id)  -- counts project rows grouped by start_year, framework_program | total_cost_sum = SUM(total_cost)  -- sum of the projects.total_cost values per group | ec_max_contribution_sum = SUM(ec_max_contribution)  -- sum of the projects.ec_max_contribution values per group
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension/look-up views that are one-row-per-key on matching keys without re-aggregation. Examples: |  - Safe: join to a programmes dimension (e.g., projects_with_programmes_subjects_topics or any programme lookup) on framework_program — safe because the view is one-row-per(start_year, framework_program) and programme lookup is one-row-per framework_program, so measures are not duplicated. |  - Safe: join to a years dimension or time table on start_year — safe because the time dimension is one-row-per start_year. |  - Safe: join to projects_rank_by_total_cost (RANK) or other views that are pre-aggregated to the same (start_year, framework_program) grain — safe when grains exactly match. | Do NOT join directly (without re-aggregation) to one-to-many downstream tables/views that expand projects into multiple rows (these WILL duplicate measures): |  - Do NOT join to project_members_clean, project_financials_by_member, projects_principal_investigators, institution_locations, project_member_counts_by_country, erc_panel_assignments, or projects_with_programmes_subjects_topics if those sibling views are at a finer grain (e.g., one row per member, per institution, per project-member) without first aggregating them to the (start_year, framework_program) grain. Doing so will multiply projects_count, total_cost_sum and ec_max_contribution_sum. | If you need to combine this view with a one-to-many view, either: |  - aggregate the one-to-many view up to (start_year, framework_program) before joining, or |  - join at the project-level by re-expanding this rollup back to individual projects (not supported from this aggregate view) — prefer joining the base projects_core (NORM) when you need project-level joins. | Notes on join keys and duplication rationale: the measures are sums/counts computed at the (start_year, framework_program) grain. Joining any table that has multiple rows per (start_year, framework_program) (for example multiple members per project or multiple locations per project) will duplicate these pre-aggregated measures unless that other table is reduced to the same grouping keys first.

projects_yearly_budget_rollup.description: Year-level aggregation of projects financials by start_year and framework_program. Produces counts and sums per year+framework suitable for trend analysis. Keeps framework_program for joins to ec_framework_programs. | Use for: Budget trends by year and framework program; Compare total_cost vs ec_max_contribution over time; Identify years with most projects per framework

projects_principal_investigators.name: projects_principal_investigators
projects_principal_investigators.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id AS unics_id,
  p.acronym AS acronym,
  p.title AS title,
  p.principal_investigator AS principal_investigator,
  pe.full_name AS principal_investigator_name
FROM projects p
LEFT JOIN people pe ON pe.unics_id = p.principal_investigator

params.description: Provides one-row-per-project basic identification and its principal investigator (PI) reference and name — useful for linking projects to PI info.
params.when_to_use: Look up a project's principal investigator ID and display name alongside project id, acronym, and title. | Filter or join projects by PI (unics_id or principal_investigator) when building higher-level reports. | Compose into aggregations or joins where you need one row per project with PI metadata as attributes (not as metrics).
params.output_schema: unics_id: project unique identifier — derived from projects.unics_id | acronym: project acronym — derived from projects.acronym | title: project title — derived from projects.title | principal_investigator: project PI person id (unics_id) — derived from projects.principal_investigator | principal_investigator_name: full name of the PI — derived from people.full_name (via LEFT JOIN on people.unics_id = projects.principal_investigator)
params.grounded_columns: projects.unics_id | projects.acronym | projects.title | projects.principal_investigator | people.unics_id | people.full_name
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a dimension that is one-row-per-project (for example projects_core on projects.unics_id) — safe because this view is one-row-per-project so joining on projects.unics_id will not duplicate rows or metrics. | Safe to join to views that are one-row-per-person keyed by people.unics_id (for example a people_core view) on principal_investigator = people.unics_id — safe because people is one-row-per-person so measures/rows in this view are not duplicated. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views such as project_members_clean, projects_with_programmes_subjects_topics, project_financials_by_member, projects_yearly_budget_rollup, project_member_counts_by_country, erc_panel_assignments, or institution_locations (if they are one-to-many) without first aggregating them to one row per projects.unics_id — joining them directly will multiply rows and thus duplicate any derived counts or sums unless you re-aggregate after the join. | If you need metrics from one-to-many siblings (e.g., total cost, member counts, programme lists), either: (a) join to an AGG sibling that is already aggregated by projects.unics_id (for example projects_yearly_budget_rollup or project_financials_by_member aggregated to projects.unics_id), or (b) aggregate the one-to-many table by projects.unics_id before joining. This preserves the one-row-per-project cardinality of this view.

projects_principal_investigators.description: Projects joined to the people table to expose principal investigator names alongside project identifiers. Useful for contacting PIs or listing PI-led projects. | Use for: List projects with PI names; Find PI workload (count projects per PI); Contact PIs for a set of projects

institution_locations.name: institution_locations
institution_locations.body_sql:
SELECT
  i.unics_id AS unics_id,
  i.institutions_name AS institutions_name,
  i.country_id AS country_id,
  c.country_name AS country_name,
  c.country_code2 AS country_code2,
  c.country_code3 AS country_code3,
  i.geocode_regions_3 AS geocode_regions_3,
  i.acronym AS acronym,
  i.short_name AS short_name,
  i.website AS website
FROM institutions i
LEFT JOIN countries c ON c.unics_id = i.country_id

params.description: Provides one-row-per-institution location details (name, country, codes, region codes, acronym, short name, website) for institutions identified by unics_id.
params.when_to_use: Lookup institution attributes (name, country, codes, website) by institution unics_id. | Enrich project- or member-level rows with institution location and metadata when joining on institution unics_id. | Compose country-level aggregations by joining this view to country or project-related tables using country_id. | Filter or group analyses by country_code2/country_code3 or geocode_regions_3 for institution cohorts.
params.output_schema: unics_id: Institution unique identifier — derived from institutions.unics_id (base column i.unics_id). | institutions_name: Official institution name — derived from institutions.institutions_name (base column i.institutions_name). | country_id: FK referencing countries.unics_id for the institution's country — derived from institutions.country_id (base column i.country_id). | country_name: Human-readable country name — derived from countries.country_name (base column c.country_name). | country_code2: ISO 2-letter country code — derived from countries.country_code2 (base column c.country_code2). | country_code3: ISO 3-letter country code — derived from countries.country_code3 (base column c.country_code3). | geocode_regions_3: Institution's 3-level geocode regions (as stored) — derived from institutions.geocode_regions_3 (base column i.geocode_regions_3). | acronym: Institution acronym — derived from institutions.acronym (base column i.acronym). | short_name: Institution short name — derived from institutions.short_name (base column i.short_name). | website: Institution website URL — derived from institutions.website (base column i.website).
params.grounded_columns: institutions.unics_id | institutions.institutions_name | institutions.country_id | institutions.geocode_regions_3 | institutions.acronym | institutions.short_name | institutions.website | countries.unics_id | countries.country_name | countries.country_code2 | countries.country_code3
params.metric: This view contains no aggregated metrics. All output columns are direct projections from base columns (no derived aggregates).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to projects_core (or any project-level view) on institution unics_id -> projects that reference an institution via the same unics_id are many-to-one (many projects per institution). Safe to join this view to project-level rows using projects_core.institution_unics_id = institution_locations.unics_id because institution_locations is one-row-per-institution and will not duplicate institution attributes. However be aware the join will repeat institution attributes per project row (expected denormalization). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to project_members_clean or projects_principal_investigators on member or investigator institution unics_id = institution_locations.unics_id — safe for enriching member/investigator rows because institution_locations is one-row-per-institution (it does not contain aggregated measures to be multiplied). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to country-level dimensions or aggregates on country_id = countries.unics_id or country_code2/country_code3 — safe because country-level tables are distinct by country and this view references exactly one country per institution. When aggregating up to country, first aggregate project/member metrics separately and then join to institution_locations on institution or country keys as appropriate. | do NOT join without re-aggregation to the following one-to-many tables/views if you intend to preserve any aggregated measures from this view (there are none) or to avoid row multiplication issues: project_financials_by_member (AGG), projects_yearly_budget_rollup (AGG), project_member_counts_by_country (AGG). These views/aggregates are one-to-many relative to an institution (they contain multiple rows per institution or per project-member), so joining them directly to institution_locations and then summing without proper grouping/re-aggregation will multiply counts/costs. Instead, either: | - join aggregated results to institution_locations on institution unics_id and treat institution_locations as a dimension (one row per institution) and aggregate the joined measures at the desired grain after the join; or | - first aggregate the one-to-many table to the institution (unics_id) grain, then join the aggregated metrics to institution_locations to avoid duplication. | do NOT join this view to another institution table/view that is one-to-many on the same institution key (e.g., an institutions_contact_points table with multiple contacts per institution) without first aggregating the contact rows to institution-level, because that would produce multiple rows per institution and duplicate attributes if not handled.

institution_locations.description: Institutions with country and region codes preserved for geospatial or regional analysis. Joins institutions to countries to expose country_name and codes. Useful for mapping institutions or grouping by country. | Use for: Count projects or members by institution country; Map institution distribution by region; Join institution data to project_members.institution_id

projects_rank_by_total_cost.name: projects_rank_by_total_cost
projects_rank_by_total_cost.body_sql:
SELECT
  unics_id,
  acronym,
  title,
  start_year,
  total_cost,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY start_year ORDER BY total_cost DESC) AS total_cost_rank_within_year
FROM projects

params.description: Ranks projects by their total_cost within each project start_year, returning project identifiers, basic metadata, the total_cost, and the rank of that cost within the same year.
params.when_to_use: Find top-N projects by total cost for a specific start year (e.g., top 10 most costly projects started in 2018). | Compare how a project's total_cost ranks relative to other projects that started the same year. | Compose year-partitioned cost rankings into dashboards or reports that combine rank with other project attributes (PI, members, programmes) without recomputing rank. | Filter or annotate project-level lists with within-year cost rank before joining to additional project-level details.
params.output_schema: unics_id: project unique identifier, derived directly from projects.unics_id | acronym: project acronym, derived directly from projects.acronym | title: project title, derived directly from projects.title | start_year: project start year (used as the rank partition key), derived directly from projects.start_year | total_cost: project-level total cost, derived directly from projects.total_cost | total_cost_rank_within_year: integer rank of total_cost within the same start_year, computed as RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY start_year ORDER BY total_cost DESC) in the view
params.metric: total_cost = projects.total_cost | total_cost_rank_within_year = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY projects.start_year ORDER BY projects.total_cost DESC)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to projects_core (or any one-row-per-unics_id view/table) on projects_rank_by_total_cost.unics_id = projects_core.unics_id — safe because both sides are one-row-per-project, so total_cost and its rank are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to projects_principal_investigators on unics_id = projects_principal_investigators.unics_id only if that view is guaranteed to be one-row-per-unics_id (e.g., one designated PI). If projects_principal_investigators can contain multiple PI rows per project, aggregate (e.g., pick primary PI or array_agg) upstream before joining to avoid duplicating total_cost and rank. | DO NOT directly join to one-to-many views/tables such as project_members_clean, project_financials_by_member, project_member_counts_by_country, projects_with_programmes_subjects_topics, projects_yearly_budget_rollup, or any other child/detail table without first either (a) aggregating the child to one row per unics_id or (b) using a join that preserves uniqueness (e.g., lateral subquery returning a single aggregated row). Directly joining these one-to-many sources will multiply rows per project and therefore multiply/duplicate total_cost and change rank semantics. | When you need combined metrics (e.g., total_cost plus aggregated member-level metrics), compose by: (1) aggregate the one-to-many table to one row per unics_id (defining the aggregation you need), and (2) join that aggregated result to projects_rank_by_total_cost on unics_id. This preserves cardinality and ensures total_cost and total_cost_rank_within_year remain correct. | When filtering by start_year, you may restrict projects_rank_by_total_cost.start_year before joining other sources to limit data volume; the partitioned rank is stable for rows in the view and will not change by downstream joins as long as you don't alter total_cost or start_year. | Avoid joining on non-unique project keys (e.g., joining on acronym or title) unless you guarantee uniqueness; always prefer unics_id as the join key to preserve the view's one-row-per-(unics_id,start_year) grain.

projects_rank_by_total_cost.description: Rank projects by total_cost within each start_year. Exposes a rank column so callers can filter downstream (e.g., top-k per year) without embedding literals here. | Use for: Select top-k most expensive projects per year (WHERE total_cost_rank_within_year <= K); Analyze distribution of project budgets within years

project_member_counts_by_country.name: project_member_counts_by_country
project_member_counts_by_country.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.project AS project,
  pm.country AS country,
  COUNT(DISTINCT pm.unics_id) AS distinct_member_count,
  SUM(pm.ec_contribution) AS total_ec_contribution_by_country
FROM project_members pm
GROUP BY pm.project, pm.country

params.description: Counts distinct project members and sums their EC contributions per project and country.
params.when_to_use: Get number of unique members and total EC contribution for each project broken down by country | Compose project-level or country-level totals by aggregating these per-project-per-country measures | Filter projects or countries before joining to other project-level dimensions without changing the meaning of the counts/amounts (if joins are cardinality-safe as described) | Build dashboards showing geographic distribution of membership and contribution within projects
params.output_schema: project: project identifier (derived from project_members.project) | country: member country code/name (derived from project_members.country) | distinct_member_count: distinct count of members for this project-country (derived from COUNT(DISTINCT project_members.unics_id)) | total_ec_contribution_by_country: sum of ec_contribution for all members in this project-country (derived from SUM(project_members.ec_contribution))
params.metric: distinct_member_count = COUNT(DISTINCT project_members.unics_id)  -- distinct members per (project, country) | total_ec_contribution_by_country = SUM(project_members.ec_contribution)  -- sum of member ec_contribution per (project, country)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to projects_core on project_members.project = projects_core.project_id — safe because this view has at most one row per (project, country) and joining to the one-row-per-project projects_core will not duplicate these rows (projects_core must be unique per project). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to projects_with_programmes_subjects_topics on project = projects_with_programmes_subjects_topics.project — safe only if that sibling view is one-row-per-project; if it is one-to-many (multiple programmes/subjects/topics per project) you must first aggregate that sibling to one row per project before joining to avoid duplicating counts and sums. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to projects_principal_investigators on project = projects_principal_investigators.project — safe only if projects_principal_investigators is one-row-per-project; if it lists multiple PIs per project, do not join directly (it will multiply this view's measures) — instead aggregate PI rows to one row per project before joining. | do NOT join directly to project_financials_by_member (one-to-many by member) without re-aggregating: joining this view to a member-level or member-transaction table will duplicate measures because project_member_counts_by_country is aggregated at (project, country) and member-level tables have multiple rows per member; if you need combined results, either (a) aggregate the member-level data to (project, country) first, or (b) join on project and country and then re-aggregate grouping by the desired grain. | do NOT join directly to institution_locations if institution_locations contains multiple location rows per institution: that would multiply rows. Aggregate or restrict institution_locations to one row per join key before joining. | safe to roll up: you can aggregate distinct_member_count and total_ec_contribution_by_country up to project-level or country-level by summing these columns because the view's grain is (project, country); to get per-project totals, sum total_ec_contribution_by_country across countries for the same project. Summing distinct_member_count across countries yields the number of distinct members per project broken down by country; note that a given member appearing in multiple countries (if possible in source data) could be double-counted — the underlying DISTINCT is per (project_members.unics_id) irrespective of country in this view's COUNT(DISTINCT), which counts unique unics_id within each (project, country). | when composing, ensure any join keys you use are at most one-to-one with this view's (project, country) rows; if the other side is one-to-many, pre-aggregate that side to (project, country) or (project) as appropriate to preserve measure correctness.

project_member_counts_by_country.description: Counts of distinct project members and sum of EC contributions grouped by project and member country. Useful for evaluating country-level participation in each project. | Use for: Which countries contributed most to a given project; Aggregate member counts by country across projects; Map financing by country within projects

erc_panel_assignments.name: erc_panel_assignments
erc_panel_assignments.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id AS unics_id,
  p.acronym AS acronym,
  pep.panel AS panel,
  ep.description AS panel_description,
  ep.part_of AS panel_part_of
FROM projects p
LEFT JOIN project_erc_panels pep ON pep.project = p.unics_id
LEFT JOIN erc_panels ep ON ep.code = pep.panel

params.description: Row-level mapping of projects to their assigned ERC panel codes and panel metadata (one row per project-panel assignment).
params.when_to_use: Find which ERC panel(s) a given project (by unics_id) was assigned to and read basic panel metadata. | Filter or group projects by ERC panel code, panel description, or panel part-of classification. | Use as a base to join project-level attributes (costs, members, PI, years) while preserving per-project-per-panel granularity.
params.output_schema: unics_id: Project unique identifier — derived from projects.unics_id (projects.unics_id AS unics_id). | acronym: Project short title/acronym — derived from projects.acronym (projects.acronym AS acronym). | panel: ERC panel code assigned to the project — derived from project_erc_panels.panel (project_erc_panels.panel AS panel). | panel_description: Human-readable description of the ERC panel code — derived from erc_panels.description (erc_panels.description AS panel_description). | panel_part_of: Higher-level grouping for the panel (if present) — derived from erc_panels.part_of (erc_panels.part_of AS panel_part_of).
params.grounded_columns: projects.unics_id | projects.acronym | project_erc_panels.project | project_erc_panels.panel | erc_panels.code | erc_panels.description | erc_panels.part_of
params.metric: note: this view exposes no aggregated measures. All columns are base attributes (no derived aggregates).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to projects_core (or any one-row-per-project dimension) on projects_core.unics_id = erc_panel_assignments.unics_id — safe because this view is at most one row per (project, panel) and projects_core is one row per project; joining keeps per-project-per-panel granularity without duplicating panel assignment rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to projects_principal_investigators on projects_principal_investigators.unics_id = erc_panel_assignments.unics_id — safe only if you intend per-project-per-panel-per-PI rows. If projects_principal_investigators is one row per project (single PI), join is safe and will not duplicate rows; if it is one-to-many (multiple PIs), this will multiply rows and should be done knowingly or after aggregation. | do NOT join without care to one-to-many tables/views such as project_members_clean, project_financials_by_member, project_member_counts_by_country, or any other member-level or transaction-level AGG/join that is one-to-many on unics_id — joining them directly will multiply erc_panel_assignments rows (one row per project-panel) by the number of member rows, thereby duplicating any measures derived from this view. Instead, either: | - aggregate the one-to-many table to one row per project (e.g., sum or count per unics_id) before joining, or | - join and then re-aggregate the combined result to the intended grain (e.g., group by panel or project and use appropriate aggregate functions). | safe-to-compose notes: because this view has no measures, duplication concerns arise only when downstream queries introduce aggregates (costs, counts). Treat erc_panel_assignments as a dimensional mapping (project -> panel) with a grain of (unics_id, panel). When composing into metrics (e.g., total cost by panel), ensure costs are taken from a source already aggregated to project-level (one row per unics_id) or use DISTINCT/unics-level aggregates to avoid double-counting when joining to member-level or multi-member financial tables. | example safe composition patterns: | - To compute total project cost by panel: join projects_yearly_budget_rollup (aggregated to unics_id) to erc_panel_assignments on unics_id, then SUM(cost) GROUP BY panel — safe because costs are pre-aggregated one row per project. | - To get number of distinct projects per panel: SELECT panel, COUNT(DISTINCT unics_id) FROM erc_panel_assignments GROUP BY panel — safe and correct. | - To add institution location data: join institution_locations only after confirming institution_locations is one-row-per-institution (and joined via an institution key), or aggregate institution_locations to the intended project granularity first.

erc_panel_assignments.description: Projects joined with their ERC panel code and panel description. Preserves project id and panel code for filtering and grouping by panel. | Use for: List projects by ERC panel; Aggregate budgets by ERC panel; Filter projects to a panel or panel group (panel_part_of)

project_principal_investigators.name: project_principal_investigators
project_principal_investigators.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id AS project_unics_id,
  p.principal_investigator AS principal_investigator,
  pe.full_name AS pi_full_name
FROM
  projects_core p
LEFT JOIN
  people pe
ON
  p.principal_investigator = pe.unics_id
project_principal_investigators.description: Mapping of a project to its principal investigator person record (if present). Useful for queries that need project + PI attributes.

project_financials_with_programme.name: project_financials_with_programme
project_financials_with_programme.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.title,
  p.total_cost,
  p.ec_max_contribution,
  p.framework_program,
  pp.programme
FROM projects_core p
LEFT JOIN projects_with_programmes_subjects_topics pp
  ON pp.unics_id = p.unics_id
project_financials_with_programme.description: Project financials combined with associated programme codes; one row per project exposing cost measures and programme membership for analysis by programme.

project_title_index.name: project_title_index
project_title_index.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  -- canonicalized title for exact or case-insensitive matching; lift literal for LOWER() locale-insensitive behavior
  lower(p.title) AS title
FROM
  projects_core p
WHERE
  p.unics_id IS NOT NULL
project_title_index.description: Simple selectable index mapping project title (canonicalized) to project id and core fields for fast exact-title lookup. Keeps one row per project and allows exact or case-insensitive title matching outside the view.

project_participants_denorm.name: project_participants_denorm
project_participants_denorm.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.project                                                   AS project,
  p.unics_id                                                   AS projects_unics_id,
  p.acronym                                                    AS projects_acronym,
  pm.unics_id                                                  AS project_member_unics_id,
  pm.member_name                                               AS project_member_name,
  pm.member_role                                               AS project_member_role,
  pm.institution_id                                            AS project_member_institution_id,
  pm.country                                                   AS project_member_country,
  i.unics_id                                                   AS institution_unics_id,
  i.institutions_name                                          AS institution_institutions_name,
  i.country_id                                                 AS institution_country_id
FROM
  project_members_clean pm
JOIN
  projects_core p
    ON pm.project = p.unics_id
LEFT JOIN
  institutions i
    ON pm.institution_id = i.unics_id
project_participants_denorm.description: Denormalized project-member/institution rows: one row per project-member combination linking projects, project_members and institutions so queries can filter projects by participant attributes (country, institution, role) and still access project identifiers/dates.

projects_time_cohort.name: projects_time_cohort
projects_time_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.acronym,
  -- lift literals: prefer canonical start_date/start_year from projects_core if present,
  -- fall back to projects.start_date / EXTRACT(year FROM projects.start_date)
  COALESCE(pc.start_date, p.start_date) AS start_date,
  COALESCE(pc.start_year, COALESCE(p.start_year, CAST(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM COALESCE(pc.start_date, p.start_date)) AS integer))) AS start_year,
  -- canonical end_date / end_year similarly
  COALESCE(pc.end_date, p.end_date) AS end_date,
  COALESCE(pc.end_year, COALESCE(p.end_year, CAST(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM COALESCE(pc.end_date, p.end_date)) AS integer))) AS end_year
FROM projects p
LEFT JOIN projects_core pc
  ON p.unics_id = pc.unics_id
projects_time_cohort.description: Project cohort view exposing projects with canonical start_date and start_year fields to support temporal filters (year, date range) and cohort selection. One row per project.

projects_row_level.name: projects_row_level
projects_row_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.acronym,
  p.title,
  p.start_date,
  p.end_date,
  p.start_year,
  p.end_year,
  p.ec_call,
  p.ec_fund_scheme,
  p.framework_program,
  p.principal_investigator
FROM
  projects_core p
projects_row_level.description: Row-level project cohort exposing primary project attributes and dates. Useful as the base cohort for filters by start/end year, acronym lookups, and joins to programme/participants.

projects_basic_for_join.name: projects_basic_for_join
projects_basic_for_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.acronym,
  -- rcn comes from project_members_clean where available (one member row per project may hold rcn)
  pm.rcn,
  p.ec_ref,
  p.framework_program,
  p.ec_fund_scheme,
  p.principal_investigator,
  p.start_date,
  p.end_date
FROM projects_core p
-- left join to project_members_clean to bring through rcn when present for the project;
-- keep at most one row per project (project_members_clean may have multiple members).
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT pm_inner.rcn
  FROM project_members_clean pm_inner
  WHERE pm_inner.project = p.unics_id
    AND pm_inner.rcn IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY pm_inner.rcn NULLS LAST
  LIMIT 1
) pm ON true
projects_basic_for_join.description: Denormalized small projects relation with identifiers and common joinable attributes (programme, principal investigator id, funding scheme) to support queries that combine project cohort with programmes, people or members.

projects_with_principal_investigator.name: projects_with_principal_investigator
projects_with_principal_investigator.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.title,
  p.start_date,
  p.principal_investigator,
  pi.full_name AS pi_full_name,
  pp.programme
FROM projects_core p
LEFT JOIN people pi
  ON pi.unics_id = p.principal_investigator
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    unics_id,
    string_agg(programme, ',' ORDER BY programme) AS programme
  FROM projects_with_programmes_subjects_topics
  GROUP BY unics_id
) pp
  ON pp.unics_id = p.unics_id
projects_with_principal_investigator.description: Project rows joined to the principal investigator person (if present) and to the programme code(s) where available; useful for queries that need project metadata plus PI or programme context.

project_members_denorm.name: project_members_denorm
project_members_denorm.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.unics_id AS "project_members.unics_id",
  pm.project AS "project_members.project",
  pm.member_name AS "project_members.member_name",
  pm.institution_id AS "project_members.institution_id",
  pm.country AS "project_members.country",
  pm.member_role AS "project_members.member_role",
  pm.ec_contribution AS "project_members.ec_contribution",
  p.unics_id AS "projects.unics_id",
  p.title AS "projects.title",
  p.start_date AS "projects.start_date",
  p.end_date AS "projects.end_date"
FROM project_members_clean pm
LEFT JOIN projects_core p
  ON pm.project = p.unics_id
project_members_denorm.description: Denormalized project-member rows linking projects to their members and member institutions; useful for filtering projects by participating institutions, countries, member roles, and contributions.

projects_with_program_and_scheme.name: projects_with_program_and_scheme
projects_with_program_and_scheme.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id AS "projects.unics_id",
  p.title AS "projects.title",
  p.start_date AS "projects.start_date",
  p.ec_fund_scheme AS "projects.ec_fund_scheme",
  fs.code AS "funding_schemes.code",
  fs.title AS "funding_schemes.title",
  p.framework_program AS "projects.framework_program",
  efp.ec_framework_program_name AS "ec_framework_programs.ec_framework_program_name"
FROM projects p
LEFT JOIN funding_schemes fs
  ON p.ec_fund_scheme = fs.code

projects_duration_metrics.name: projects_duration_metrics
projects_duration_metrics.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.start_year,
  p.end_year,
  -- duration in years as a fractional number: difference in days divided by 365.25
  -- Lifted literals: 365.25 used for average year length including leap years
  CASE
    WHEN p.start_date IS NULL AND p.end_date IS NULL AND p.start_year IS NOT NULL AND p.end_year IS NOT NULL
      THEN ( (p.end_year::numeric + 0.0) - (p.start_year::numeric + 0.0) )
    WHEN p.start_date IS NULL AND p.start_year IS NOT NULL AND p.end_date IS NOT NULL
      THEN ( (p.end_date - make_date(p.start_year, 1, 1)) / 365.25 )
    WHEN p.end_date IS NULL AND p.end_year IS NOT NULL AND p.start_date IS NOT NULL
      THEN ( (make_date(p.end_year, 12, 31) - p.start_date) / 365.25 )
    WHEN p.start_date IS NOT NULL AND p.end_date IS NOT NULL
      THEN ( (p.end_date - p.start_date) / 365.25 )
    WHEN p.start_date IS NULL AND p.end_date IS NULL AND p.start_year IS NULL AND p.end_year IS NOT NULL
      THEN ( (p.end_year::numeric + 0.0) - (p.end_year::numeric + 0.0) )  -- zero duration fallback
    WHEN p.start_date IS NULL AND p.end_date IS NULL AND p.start_year IS NOT NULL AND p.end_year IS NULL
      THEN ( (p.start_year::numeric + 0.0) - (p.start_year::numeric + 0.0) )  -- zero duration fallback
    ELSE NULL
  END AS duration_years
FROM projects_core p
projects_duration_metrics.description: Aggregated metrics per project computing duration in years and exposing it as a measure to enable ranking and max-duration queries. Grain is project-level (one row per project).
